title: Appeal Level Chart for Insurance Coverage & Claims Payer Classes
content:
Each payer class under **Insurance Coverage & Claims** names its first appeal level in its own words and sets its own filing windows. The chart lists them.

## Level names and first-level window

| Payer class | Payer's name for the first appeal level | First-level window (calendar days after the denial notice date) | Days added to the notice date for presumed receipt |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | Redetermination | 120 | 5 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | Plan Reconsideration | 60 | 0 |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | Follows the Medicare determination | 0 (no separate appeal) | 0 |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | Plan Appeal | 60 | 0 |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | Reconsideration | 90 | 0 |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | Internal Appeal | 180 | 0 |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | Member Appeal by Authorized Representative | 180 | 0 |

## Later levels

| Payer class | Second-level window (calendar days after the first-level decision) | Upheld first level forwarded to the second level automatically | Third-level window (calendar days after the second-level decision) | Minimum amount still in dispute for a third-level request (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 180 | No | 60 | 190.00 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | 0 | Yes | 60 | 190.00 |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | 0 (none) | No | 0 (none) | 0.00 |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | 120 | No | 0 (none) | 0.00 |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | 60 | No | 60 | 300.00 |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | 60 | No | 120 | 0.00 |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | 60 | No | 120 | 0.00 |

## Chart notes

- A second-level window of 0 means there is no second level or that it is automatic; for the Medicare Advantage Plan it is automatic, the payer forwarding an upheld first level itself.
- A minimum of 0.00 means the payer class sets no minimum amount in controversy for the third level.
- The third level is the ALJ, hearing or external review request, whichever the payer class provides.

## Day-count examples (hypothetical denial dates)

- **Original Medicare Part B.** The first-level window is 120 days plus the 5 days of presumed receipt, 125 calendar days in all. With the denial notice date as day 0, a Redetermination filed on day 125 is within the window; one filed on day 126 is not.
- **Commercial In-Network Plan.** No receipt days are added, so the Internal Appeal window is 180 calendar days: day 180 is within it, day 181 is not.
